claim: T2N is a powerful interface to control NEURON with Matlab and TREES toolbox.
source: Here, we present T2N, a powerful interface to control NEURON with Matlab and TREES toolbox, which supports generating models stable over a broad range of reconstructed and synthetic morphologies.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the developed tool.

claim: T2N supports generating models stable over a broad range of reconstructed and synthetic morphologies.
source: Here, we present T2N, a powerful interface to control NEURON with Matlab and TREES toolbox, which supports generating models stable over a broad range of reconstructed and synthetic morphologies.

claim: The active model of dentate granule cells replicates a wide palette of experiments from various labs.
source: We illustrate this for a novel, highly detailed active model of dentate granule cells (GCs) replicating a wide palette of experiments from various labs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental validations shown in Figures 3-8 and Tables 1-3.

claim: The model reproduces data from mouse or rat, mature or adult-born GCs as well as pharmacological interventions and epileptic conditions by implementing known differences in ion channel composition and morphology.
source: By implementing known differences in ion channel composition and morphology, our model reproduces data from mouse or rat, mature or adult-born GCs as well as pharmacological interventions and epileptic conditions.
evidence: This is demonstrated through multiple figures showing comparisons between model and experimental data across different conditions.

claim: Neurons have long been interpreted as passive integrators of input signals that fire action potentials when a threshold is reached.
source: Traditionally, neurons have long been interpreted as passive integrators of input signals that fire action potentials when a threshold is reached (Knight, 1972).
evidence: This is a historical perspective cited from Knight, 1972.

claim: The output of neurons depends on many intrinsic cellular mechanisms including voltage-gated channels, dendritic architecture, synaptic plasticity, active dendrites, and axon initial segment.
source: This paradigm has meanwhile changed as the output of neurons was shown to depend on many intrinsic cellular mechanisms (e.g. voltage-gated channels, dendritic architecture, synaptic plasticity, active dendrites, axon initial segment) indicating that single neuron computation is rather complex (Softky and Koch, 1993; Brunel et al., 2014; Volgushev, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: Single neuron computation is rather complex.
source: This paradigm has meanwhile changed as the output of neurons was shown to depend on many intrinsic cellular mechanisms (e.g. voltage-gated channels, dendritic architecture, synaptic plasticity, active dendrites, axon initial segment) indicating that single neuron computation is rather complex (Softky and Koch, 1993; Brunel et al., 2014; Volgushev, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Detailed compartmental models have found their way into the set of tools for neuroscientists to understand, test, or predict mechanisms underlying neuronal function.
source: Consequently, detailed compartmental models have found their way into the set of tools for neuroscientists to understand, test, or predict mechanisms underlying neuronal function (de Schutter, 1994).
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by a citation.

claim: Most published models behave poorly when used outside of the scope for which they were created.
source: However, most published models behave poorly when used outside of the scope for which they were created.
evidence: This is a critical observation that motivates the development of T2N.

claim: Reasons for poor model performance include bona fide adaptation of other models without knowing their limitations, too few target constraints, no scientific rationale for setting parameters, missing axon initial segments, and lack of pharmacology data.
source: There are several reasons for this, such as bona fide adaptation of other models without knowing their limitations, too few target constraints because of using a low number of target parameters, no scientific rationale for setting the parameters, missing axon initial segments and a lack of data from pharmacology to fit and test the model's individual components (Almog and Korngreen, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Almog and Korngreen, 2016.

claim: Model neurons often contain a mix of constraints from very different experimental conditions and animals, combined in sometimes inconsistent ways.
source: Furthermore, model neurons often contain a mix of constraints from very different experimental conditions and animals, combined in sometimes inconsistent ways.
evidence: This is a general observation about the state of the field.

claim: T2N enables design of detailed electrophysiology models on the basis of large datasets of reconstructed and synthetic morphologies rather than single morphologies.
source: T2N enables to design detailed electrophysiology models on the basis not of single morphologies but rather on large datasets of reconstructed and synthetic morphologies.
evidence: This is a key feature of T2N demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: Morphological datasets have become more easily available from online databases such as NeuroMorpho.Org.
source: Such datasets have become more easily available from online databases such as NeuroMorpho.Org (Ascoli et al., 2007) and morphological modeling studies (Cuntz et al., 2008, 2010; Koene et al., 2009; Beining et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant databases and studies.

claim: Ion channel models from newly available databases can be directly incorporated into T2N models.
source: In addition, ion channel models from newly available databases (Ranjan et al., 2011; Podlaski et al., 2016; McDougal et al., 2017) can be directly incorporated into T2N models to consider the many new insights from recent studies on neuronal electrophysiology and protein expression.
evidence: This is a stated capability of T2N supported by citations to relevant databases.

claim: The novel compartmental models are solely based on ion channel isoforms known to exist in the neurons of interest.
source: Through this tool, we aimed here to create novel compartmental models that (1) are solely based on ion channel isoforms known to exist in the neurons of interest, (2) are robust over many different real and synthetic dendritic morphologies and (3) reproduce experimental results from various studies.
evidence: This is a stated goal and achievement of the modeling approach, supported by Table 1 and extensive literature review.

claim: The novel compartmental models are robust over many different real and synthetic dendritic morphologies.
source: Through this tool, we aimed here to create novel compartmental models that (1) are solely based on ion channel isoforms known to exist in the neurons of interest, (2) are robust over many different real and synthetic dendritic morphologies and (3) reproduce experimental results from various studies.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figures 3-8 showing consistent results across different morphologies.

claim: The novel compartmental models reproduce experimental results from various studies.
source: Through this tool, we aimed here to create novel compartmental models that (1) are solely based on ion channel isoforms known to exist in the neurons of interest, (2) are robust over many different real and synthetic dendritic morphologies and (3) reproduce experimental results from various studies.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout the Results section with comparisons to experimental data.

claim: Hippocampal dentate granule cells play a crucial role in learning and memory.
source: Although T2N can be used to create robust models for any neuron type, in this work we focused on hippocampal dentate granule cells, which play a crucial role in learning and memory and exhibit the unique feature that they integrate into the adult hippocampal network as newborn neurons throughout life.
evidence: This is established knowledge about dentate granule cells.

claim: Dentate granule cells exhibit the unique feature that they integrate into the adult hippocampal network as newborn neurons throughout life.
source: Although T2N can be used to create robust models for any neuron type, in this work we focused on hippocampal dentate granule cells, which play a crucial role in learning and memory and exhibit the unique feature that they integrate into the adult hippocampal network as newborn neurons throughout life.
evidence: This refers to adult neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus, which is well-established.

claim: T2N makes maximal use of region specifications that are available in TREES toolbox for insertion of biophysical mechanisms.
source: For the insertion of biophysical mechanisms, T2N makes maximal use of region specifications that are available in TREES toolbox.
evidence: This is a design feature of T2N described in the manuscript.

claim: Handling of section lists in NEURON is not necessary when using T2N.
source: Handling of section lists in NEURON is not necessary.
evidence: This is a stated advantage of using T2N.

claim: T2N enables an easy and efficient switch among diverse morphologies from different species.
source: For a given set of biophysical mechanisms, T2N enables an easy and efficient switch among diverse morphologies from different species including any number of morphologies downloaded from for example, databases of reconstructed morphologies such as NeuroMorpho.Org.
evidence: This capability is demonstrated in the manuscript by switching between mouse and rat morphologies.

claim: T2N facilitates the generalization of predictions from one dendritic tree type to other types.
source: This facilitates the generalization of predictions from one dendritic tree type to other types and supports the search for universal principles valid for all dendritic morphologies.
evidence: This is a stated benefit of T2N's design.

claim: T2N provides a simple and clear set up and controls NEURON compartmental models with a direct subsequent analysis with Matlab and the TREES toolbox.
source: T2N provides a simple and clear set up and controls NEURON compartmental models with a direct subsequent analysis with Matlab and the TREES toolbox allowing for any morphology related analyses.
evidence: This is a core feature of T2N described in the manuscript.

claim: T2N enhances the readability and compatibility of the code by generating stereotyped NEURON scripts.
source: By generating stereotyped NEURON scripts, T2N enhances the readability and compatibility of the code.
evidence: This is a stated advantage of T2N's approach.

claim: Multiple simulations are run automatically in parallel on different cores without the need of rewriting the NEURON code.
source: Multiple simulations are run automatically in parallel on different cores without the need of rewriting the NEURON code.
evidence: This is a technical feature of T2N described in the manuscript.

claim: T2N supports parallel NEURON and distributes cells automatically on a given amount of cores, thereby increasing the speed of large-scale network simulations drastically.
source: When activated, T2N also supports parallel NEURON (Migliore et al., 2006; Hines and Carnevale, 2008) and distributes cells automatically on a given amount of cores, thereby increasing the speed of large-scale network simulations drastically.
evidence: This is a stated capability of T2N with citations to parallel NEURON.

claim: T2N makes it easier to plot and visualize the results of simulations and their analysis by connecting NEURON to Matlab.
source: By connecting NEURON to Matlab, T2N makes it easier to plot and visualize the results of simulations and their analysis.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1C and throughout the manuscript.

claim: T2N provides users with powerful tools for an in-depth analysis of structure-function relationships in neurons by coupling morphological software and compartmental simulations.
source: In summary, by coupling morphological software and compartmental simulations, T2N provides users with powerful tools for an in-depth analysis of structure-function relationships in neurons.
evidence: This is a summary statement about T2N's capabilities.

claim: T2N simplifies distributing dendritic, somatic and axonal ion channels in layer- or branch-specific manner.
source: T2N simplifies distributing dendritic, somatic and axonal ion channels in layer- or branch-specific manner.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2A and Table 1.

claim: The GC model includes only those channel isoforms which were described for GCs.
source: Importantly, we included only those channel isoforms, which were described for GCs.

claim: Compartment-specific distributions of the channels were implemented according to immunohistochemical labeling and light or electron microscopy as well as electrophysiological data.
source: Moreover, we carefully implemented compartment-specific distributions of the channels according to immunohistochemical labeling and light or electron microscopy as well as electrophysiological data (Table 1 and Figure 2A).

claim: Available tools of NEURON have limitations with regard to specifying layer- or branch-specific biophysical properties in a large dataset of morphologies.
source: Available tools of NEURON have limitations with regard to specifying layer- or branch-specific biophysical properties in a large dataset of morphologies.
evidence: This is a stated limitation that T2N addresses.

claim: T2N makes it easy to insert ion channels in selected regions because it maps the nodes, branches and regions of the TREES toolbox onto sections and segments in NEURON.
source: T2N makes it easy to insert ion channels in selected regions because it maps the nodes, branches and regions of the TREES toolbox (Cuntz et al., 2010, 2011) onto sections and segments in NEURON (see Tutorial 1 in Appendix 1).

claim: The morphological model is capable of reproducing detailed morphological parameters of reconstructed mouse GCs.
source: We developed a morphological mouse model capable of reproducing detailed morphological parameters of reconstructed mouse GCs (Schmidt-Hieber et al., 2007).

claim: The resulting synthetic dendritic trees were morphologically comparable to the reconstructed trees of mouse GCs from Schmidt-Hieber et al. (2007).
source: The resulting synthetic dendritic trees were morphologically comparable to the reconstructed trees of mouse GCs from Schmidt-Hieber et al. (2007) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C,D with quantitative comparisons.

claim: The GC model is able to reproduce passive properties, steady state currents as well as AP shape and spiking behavior observed in patch-clamp experiments.
source: Figure 3 (middle column) and Table 2 show the results of such simulations in morphologies of mature GCs (for details see Appendix 2) indicating that our model is able to reproduce passive properties, steady state currents as well as AP shape and spiking behavior observed in patch-clamp experiments (Figure 3, left column; Mongiat et al., 2009).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3 and Table 2 with comparisons to experimental data.

claim: The GC model remained stable and continued to generate realistic electrophysiological traces even after replacing reconstructed dendrites with synthetic dendrites while keeping all biophysical mechanisms unaltered.
source: Importantly, the GC model remained stable and continued to generate realistic electrophysiological traces even after replacing one set of GC morphologies (reconstructed dendrites) by a different set of morphologies (synthetic dendrites; Figure 3, right column; see also Appendix 2) while keeping all biophysical mechanisms unaltered.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3 comparing middle and right columns.

claim: The insertion of different morphologies introduced certain amount of variability in electrophysiological behavior.
source: Interestingly, the insertion of different morphologies introduced certain amount of variability in electrophysiological behavior (see Appendix 2 for details).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Some of the variance observed in electrophysiological recordings might be explained by the morphological variability of GCs.
source: Thus, some of the variance observed in electrophysiological recordings might be explained by the morphological variability of GCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed variability in the model.

claim: Increasing the Kir conductance was sufficient to replicate mature rat GC I-V recordings using rat morphologies.
source: Interestingly, increasing the Kir conductance (see Appendix 2 for details) was sufficient to replicate mature rat GC I-V recordings (Pourbadie et al., 2015) using rat morphologies (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4B.

claim: After the adjustment of the Kir conductance, active channel properties and densities from mouse GCs reproduced the spiking behavior of rat GCs.
source: Also, after the adjustment of the Kir conductance, active channel properties and densities from mouse GCs (Table 1) reproduced the spiking behavior of rat GCs (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4C-D.

claim: Both rodent species might share a similar GC ionic channel density pattern, conferring to these neurons their electrophysiological identity.
source: This result indicates that both rodent species might share a similar GC ionic channel density pattern, conferring to these neurons their electrophysiological identity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful transfer of the model between species.

claim: Real and synthetic rat morphologies could be interchanged without affecting the spiking behavior.
source: Similarly to the mouse GC model, we could interchange real and synthetic rat morphologies without affecting the spiking behavior (Figure 4B–D, left vs. right).

claim: The active model shows inherent robustness and validates its usefulness for large-scale network simulations of the rat DG.
source: This shows an inherent robustness of our active model and validates its usefulness for large-scale network simulations of the rat DG.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the demonstrated robustness across morphologies.

claim: The rat GC model was able to reproduce bAP attenuation determined from dendritic patch clamp experiments.
source: The rat GC model was able to reproduce bAP attenuation (Figure 5A, left; see Appendix 2 for details) determined from dendritic patch clamp experiments (Krueppel et al., 2011).

source: Interestingly, for a realistic delay of the bAP peak, we had to adjust the specific axial resistance Ra and the passive membrane conductance to the higher temperature of 33°C (Figure 5B, left) that was used in experiments (Krueppel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5B.

claim: The phenomenological Ca2+ buffer model generated realistic intracellular Ca2+ signals induced by bAPs.
source: Moreover, we used a well-tuned phenomenological Ca2+ buffer model (see Appendix 2 for details), which generated realistic intracellular Ca2+ signals induced by bAPs (Figure 5C, left).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5C with comparison to experimental data.

claim: Ca2+ dynamics in synthetic morphologies matched Ca2+ signals from experiments as well as those from reconstructed morphologies.
source: Ca2+ dynamics in synthetic morphologies (Figure 5C, green bars) matched Ca2+ signals from experiments (black bars) as well as those from reconstructed morphologies (blue bars).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The GC model generated realistic and stable intracellular Ca2+ dynamics over a broad range of different morphologies in rat and mouse.
source: Thus, our GC model generated realistic and stable intracellular Ca2+ dynamics over a broad range of different morphologies in rat and mouse.

claim: The model predicted that bAP attenuation was smaller in mouse GCs than in rat GCs.
source: The model predicted that bAP attenuation was smaller in mouse GCs than in rat GCs.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A comparing left and right panels.

claim: Ca2+ levels in mouse GCs were comparable to Ca2+ levels in rat GCs.
source: Ca2+ levels in mouse GCs were comparable to Ca2+ levels in rat GCs.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Dendritic Ca2+ signaling is relatively similar in both species despite differences in backpropagating dendritic voltage spread, provided that Ca2+ buffering and extrusion mechanisms are comparable between mouse and rat GCs.
source: Provided that Ca2+ buffering and extrusion mechanisms are comparable between mouse and rat GCs (Stocca et al., 2008), this suggests that dendritic Ca2+ signaling is relatively similar in both species despite differences in backpropagating dendritic voltage spread.
evidence: This is an inference based on the model predictions with a conditional assumption.

claim: T2N helps identify crucial parameters affecting electrophysiological behavior of compartmental models because it supports flexible whole cell as well region- and layer-specific manipulations of ion channel properties.
source: T2N helps identify crucial parameters affecting electrophysiological behavior of compartmental models because it supports flexible whole cell as well region- and layer-specific manipulations of ion channel properties.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6 and Tutorial 8.

claim: The model GCs exhibited similar changes to protective upregulation of HCN and Kir or Kv1.1 channels observed during temporal lobe epilepsy.
source: As shown previously in experiments, protective upregulation of HCN and Kir (Young et al., 2009; Stegen et al., 2012) or Kv1.1 channels (Kirchheim et al., 2013) decreases GC excitability under epilepsy conditions. In line with these data, our model GCs exhibited similar changes (Figure 6D,E; see also Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and Appendix 2 for further details).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6D,E with comparison to experimental findings.

claim: T2N can be used to estimate effects of pathology-related alterations, which are robust across multiple non-identical single-cell morphologies.
source: This shows that T2N can be used to estimate effects of pathology-related alterations, which are robust across multiple non-identical single-cell morphologies.

claim: Changing the expression of Kir2 channels and other channel types led to altered I-V curves and increased excitability in young abGCs as compared to mature GCs, in line with experimental findings.

evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 7 with comparison to experimental data.

claim: The robust compartmental models generated using T2N can easily be adapted for exploring varying electrophysiological states of the same cell type, for example, during adult neurogenesis and potentially also during development.

claim: When abGCs were driven by a smaller number of synapses, they exhibited similar synaptic input/output relationships as mGCs.
source: Importantly, when abGCs were driven by a smaller number of synapses, they exhibited similar synaptic input/output relationships as mGCs (Figure 8A).

claim: Higher intrinsic excitability of abGCs compensates for their lower numbers of synaptic inputs.
source: This suggests that higher intrinsic excitability of abGCs (see also Figure 7C) compensates for their lower numbers of synaptic inputs.

claim: Both young abGCs and mature GCs are tuned to follow input frequencies in the theta range (<10 Hz).
source: Moreover, our modeling indicates that both young abGCs and mature GCs are tuned to follow input frequencies in the theta range (<10 Hz; Figure 8B).

claim: Diminished glutamatergic input is compensated by the enhanced excitability when GABAergic inhibition is blocked.
source: This result is consistent with studies showing that diminished glutamatergic input is compensated by the enhanced excitability when GABAergic inhibition is blocked (Mongiat et al., 2009; Pardi et al., 2015).

claim: Young abGCs were more efficiently activated by temporally separated (>15 ms) incoming activity from medial and lateral perforant path inputs as compared to mature GCs.
source: Furthermore, despite their weaker excitatory input, we found that young abGCs were more efficiently activated by temporally separated (>15 ms) incoming activity from medial and lateral perforant path inputs as compared to mature GCs.

source: Our model predicts that at low frequencies in the theta range, young abGCs were able to integrate synaptic inputs with a broader time window than mGCs (Figure 8B and Appendix 2).

claim: The broader tuning of abGCs is in line with the proposed special role of abGCs in hippocampal pattern separation and integration.
source: This is in line with the proposed special role of abGCs in hippocampal pattern separation and integration due to their broader tuning to the activity of synaptic inputs (Aimone et al., 2010; Johnston et al., 2016; Rangel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The model reproduces and predicts the activation patterns of young and mature granule cells under those conditions when inhibition is not present.
source: In conclusion, our model reproduces and predicts the activation patterns of young and mature granule cells under those conditions when inhibition is not present.

source: In summary, T2N is a versatile and adaptable tool for extensive in silico structure-function analyses in NEURON.

source: Interestingly, the resulting electrophysiological variability was in the range of experimental data indicating that morphological variability is able to account for a large part of electrophysiological variability.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of model and experimental variability.

claim: The model provides a valuable tool to create a DG network model with thousands of different but realistic GC morphologies and data-driven GC spiking behavior.
source: Hence, our model provides a valuable tool to create a DG network model with thousands of different but realistic GC morphologies (c.f. Schneider et al., 2012; Schneider et al., 2014) and data-driven GC spiking behavior.
evidence: This is a stated application of the model.

claim: Biophysical mechanisms were based on detailed, up-to-date knowledge of the ion channel distribution and kinetics.
source: One important reason is that our biophysical mechanisms were based on detailed, up-to-date knowledge of the ion channel distribution and kinetics.
evidence: This is documented in Table 1 with extensive references.

claim: Both morphological as well as biophysical model parameters were determined in a species-, cell type- and cell-age-specific manner.
source: Second, both morphological as well as biophysical model parameters were determined in a species-, cell type- and cell-age-specific manner.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the separate models for mouse, rat, mature, and young GCs.

claim: The model was tuned using a large set of realistic dendritic trees instead of using one morphology or simplified morphologies.
source: Third, instead of using one morphology or simplified morphologies, we tuned the model using a large set of realistic dendritic trees.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: Realistic intracellular Ca2+ dynamics were implemented so that unrealistic Ca2+- or Ca2+-dependent channel densities did not have to be used.
source: Fourth, because we implemented realistic intracellular Ca2+ dynamics we did not have to use unrealistic Ca2+- or Ca2+-dependent channel densities (for details see Appendix 2).
evidence: This is a stated advantage of the modeling approach.

claim: Several traces and datasets were used to tune the model instead of using a single voltage trace or a single recording.
source: Fifth, instead of using a single voltage trace or a single recording, we used several traces and datasets to tune the model.
evidence: This is evident from the multiple experimental comparisons throughout the manuscript.

claim: By reproducing numerous electrophysiological phenotypes rather than one phenotype, the approach was similar to a multiple objective approach.
source: By reproducing numerous electrophysiological phenotypes rather than one phenotype, our approach was similar to a multiple objective approach of Druckmann et al. (2007).
evidence: This is a comparison to another modeling approach with a citation.

claim: A single solution was found that works across many morphologies, not a set of solutions with different parameter combinations for each morphology.
source: Of note, we found a single solution that works across many morphologies, not a set of solutions with different parameter combinations for each morphology.
evidence: This is a key finding about the robustness of the model.

claim: The work suggests that morphologic robustness arises naturally in models in which parameters have been tuned using multiple different experiments and morphologies.
source: Taken together, our work suggests that morphologic robustness arises naturally in models in which parameters have been tuned using multiple different experiments and morphologies.
evidence: This is a general conclusion from the work.

claim: The Aradi and Holmes GC model failed to reproduce electrophysiological data after transferring it to diverse mouse and rat GC morphologies.
source: This conclusion is also supported by a comparison of our biophysical model to an earlier widely used GC model from Aradi and Holmes (1999) (e.g. Schneider et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2014; Mateos-Aparicio, Murphy and Storm, 2014; Jedlicka et al., 2015; Platschek et al., 2016), which failed to reproduce electrophysiological data after transferring it to diverse mouse and rat GC morphologies (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated in the supplementary figures.

claim: The community of computational neuroscientists should start to build models which perform well outside of the scope for which they were created.
source: We believe that now the community of computational neuroscientists should start to build models, which perform well outside of the scope, for which they were created (Almog and Korngreen, 2016).
evidence: This is a recommendation for the field.

claim: Mature rat GCs display a reduced excitability due to incorporation of additional Kir channels.
source: Our results suggest that mature rat GCs display a reduced excitability due to incorporation of additional Kir channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling results in Figure 4.

claim: The increased leak conductance in the rat GC model improved the fitting of simulated bAP attenuation to physiological recordings obtained from rat experiments.
source: In line with this, the increased leak conductance in the rat GC model improved the fitting of simulated bAP attenuation to physiological recordings obtained from rat experiments (Krueppel et al., 2011), as the attenuation was too weak in the unmodified rat model (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the modeling.

claim: Adult-born GC development is similar to postnatal GC development.
source: To implement these changes we used data on ion channels which are known to be upregulated during postnatal development (Table 3) assuming that adult-born is similar to postnatal GC development (Espósito et al., 2005; Zhao et al., 2006; Snyder et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an assumption supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The abGC model predicts that the beta4 subunit is less expressed or not associated with BK channels in young abGCs.
source: Thus, the abGC model predicts that the beta4 subunit is less expressed or not associated with BK channels in young abGCs.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the modeling results.

claim: Future improvements of the abGC model should focus on more realistic simulations of details in voltage traces including fAHP kinetics.
source: Future improvements of the abGC model should focus on more realistic simulations of details in voltage traces including fAHP kinetics, which are reproduced qualitatively but not quantitatively by the current model (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a stated limitation and direction for future work.

claim: Diminished glutamatergic input onto abGCs was compensated by their enhanced excitability when GABAergic inhibition was absent, in line with experimental data.
source: In line with experimental data (Mongiat et al., 2009; Pardi et al., 2015), we found that diminished glutamatergic input onto abGCs was compensated by their enhanced excitability when GABAergic inhibition was absent.
evidence: This is a finding from the model supported by citations to experimental data.

claim: Both populations of GCs responded in a similar fashion over a wide range of stimuli, which is in agreement with electrophysiological recordings.
source: Both populations of GCs responded in a similar fashion over a wide range of stimuli, which is also in agreement with electrophysiological recordings (Pardi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the model supported by a citation.

claim: T2N can be used to model also younger abGC at various ages by coupling different phases of dendrite development to corresponding biophysical models.
source: However, T2N can be used to model also younger abGC at various ages. By coupling different phases of dendrite development to corresponding biophysical models, T2N may reveal the principles, which support the maintenance of structural and functional integrity of real or synthetic morphologies as they mature or change during pathology (see Narayanan and Chattarji, 2010; Dhupia et al., 2014; Bozelos et al., 2015; Platschek et al., 2016; Platschek et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a stated potential application of T2N.

claim: Most existing GC models did not implement specific ion channels but instead used equations describing ion currents that had been measured in GCs.
source: Most existing GC models did not implement specific ion channels but instead used equations describing ion currents (A-, M-, T-type, L-type, N-type, delayed rectifier etc.) that had been measured in GCs, but which are formed by the combined action of several differently distributed ion channels in the real cell (e.g. Kv1 and Kv4 form the A-type current in GCs but are localized in the axon or dendrite, respectively).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous modeling approaches.

claim: By incorporating the contributions of different ion channel isoforms, the model can be used to analyze and predict the impact of different channelopathies or compensatory ion channel adaptations onto the cell's active and passive behavior.
source: By incorporating the contributions of different ion channel isoforms, our model can be used to analyze and predict the impact of different channelopathies or compensatory ion channel adaptations onto the cell's active and passive behavior.
evidence: This is a stated application of the model.

claim: Specific isoforms dynamically control excitability and alter their expression under pathological conditions such as epilepsy or oxidative stress.
source: This might be of special interest since specific isoforms dynamically control excitability (e.g. Kv2.1; Misonou et al., 2005) and alter their expression under pathological conditions such as epilepsy (e.g. Kv1.1; Kirchheim et al., 2013; or Kir2.1 and HCN; Stegen et al., 2012) or oxidative stress (e.g. Kv4; Rüschenschmidt et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The model was able to reproduce qualitatively the effects of a compensatory upregulation of Kir, HCN and Kv1.1 channels reported in TLE demonstrating its predictive power.
source: Indeed, our model was able to reproduce qualitatively the effects of a compensatory upregulation of Kir, HCN and Kv1.1 channels reported in TLE (Stegen et al., 2012; Kirchheim et al., 2013) demonstrating its predictive power there.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6D,E.

claim: The model might be used to predict single or combined effects of other TLE-induced hippocampal alterations.
source: Thus, the model might further be used to predict single or combined effects of other TLE-induced hippocampal alterations such as the reduction of BK channels in GCs (Pacheco Otalora et al., 2008), the aberrant connectivity (see review by Sharma et al., 2007; and network model by Santhakumar et al., 2005), as well as the impact of therapeutic gene transfer approaches, such as the transfer of the K2P leak channel TREK-1 to ameliorate status epilepticus (Dey et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a stated potential application of the model.

claim: A different channel density distribution might result in a similarly robust and successful reproduction of experimental results, as the entire parameter space was not investigated.
source: As we did not investigate the entire parameter space of our electrophysiological models (especially in the young abGC model), for example using a genetic algorithm, we cannot exclude that a different channel density distribution would result in a similarly robust and successful reproduction of experimental results (Achard and De Schutter, 2006).
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation.

claim: Previous work in other cell types and animals has shown that similar electrical behavior might arise from different combinations and parameters of ion channels.
source: However, previous work in other cell types and animals has shown that similar electrical behavior might arise from different combinations and parameters of ion channels (Achard and De Schutter, 2006; Günay et al., 2008; Prinz et al., 2004; for review see Marder, 2011; Marder and Goaillard, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature on degeneracy.

claim: Future versions of T2N should make it possible to reconstruct, build and simulate astrocytes and astrocyte-neuron interactions.
source: As other cellular interactions, such as astrocytic-neuronal contacts are emerging to play an important role, e.g. for meta-plasticity (Abraham and Bear, 1996; Abraham, 2008), future versions of T2N should make it possible to reconstruct, build and simulate astrocytes and astrocyte-neuron interactions.
evidence: This is a stated direction for future development.

claim: The set of T2N functions can be extended to simplify modeling of new experimental settings including simulations of nonlinear synaptic integration or synaptic and intrinsic plasticity as well as structural dendritic plasticity.
source: The set of T2N functions can be extended to simplify modeling of new experimental settings including simulations of nonlinear synaptic integration or synaptic and intrinsic plasticity as well as structural dendritic plasticity such as dendritic retraction or pruning of dendritic segments (Beining et al., 2017; Platschek et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a stated direction for future development.

claim: Including stochastic sampling algorithms would make T2N suitable to study degeneracy by supporting a search for distinct combinations of morphological and biophysical properties generating similar physiological outcomes.
source: Including stochastic sampling algorithms would make T2N suitable to study degeneracy by supporting a search for distinct combinations of morphological and biophysical properties generating similar physiological outcomes.
evidence: This is a stated direction for future development.

claim: The model is of high predictive value for studies on the single-cell and network behavior of mature GCs and young abGCs, as well as under pathological conditions.
source: Therefore, it is of high predictive value for studies on the single-cell and network behavior of mature GCs and young abGCs, as well as under pathological conditions of synaptic, morphological or physiological alterations of GCs.
evidence: This is a stated significance of the model.

claim: The model satisfies the objective constraints from experiments and is robust to experimentally verifiable manipulations.
source: Nevertheless, our model satisfies the objective constraints from experiments (Table 2) and is robust to experimentally verifiable manipulations.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout the Results section.

claim: The main point is the emphasis on using many different morphologies in combination with carefully, biologically constrained ion channel models.
source: Our main point is the emphasis on using many different morphologies in combination with carefully, biologically constrained ion channel models.
evidence: This is a key message of the manuscript.

claim: It is likely that the complete GC ion channel set offers redundancy and stability with respect to differences such as in morphology or species.
source: While one reason for the particular robustness of our model comes from the modeling approach using T2N, it is likely that the complete GC ion channel set offers redundancy and stability with respect to differences such as in morphology or species.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the biological basis of model robustness.

claim: It will be interesting to further investigate whether the redundancy introduced by the set of existing ion channels is responsible for the robustness to morphological modifications in the GC model.
source: Therefore, it will be interesting to further investigate whether the redundancy introduced by the set of existing ion channels is responsible for the robustness to morphological modifications in our GC model.
evidence: This is a stated direction for future research.

claim: The biophysical and morphological model provides a basis for future studies determining how cell-to-cell and animal-to-animal variability of ion channel expression combined with morphological and synaptic variability affects the robustness of GC passive and active behavior.
source: Thus, our biophysical and morphological model provides a basis for future studies determining how cell-to-cell and animal-to-animal variability of ion channel expression combined with morphological and synaptic variability affects the robustness of GC passive and active behavior.
evidence: This is a stated application for future research.

claim: The model can now be used to address the question whether ion channel degeneracy in GCs exists in terms of compensatory interactions between multiple ion channels and how it contributes to the homeostasis of GC function.
source: Our model is available on the ModelDB public database (http://senselab.med.yale.edu/ModelDB/default.asp) and can now be used to address the exciting question whether ion channel degeneracy in GCs exists in terms of compensatory interactions between multiple ion channels (Drion et al., 2015) and how it contributes to the homeostasis of GC function.
evidence: This is a stated application of the model.

claim: Future work should address whether variation of some other biological factors besides morphology or in addition to it would also lead to robust GC simulation results.
source: Future work should also address the question whether variation of some other biological factors besides morphology or in addition to it would also lead to robust GC simulation results.
evidence: This is a stated direction for future research.

claim: T2N could be extended by incorporating stochastic search algorithms to generate multiple randomized models with different biophysical and morphological parameters leading to similar electrophysiological behavior.
source: As mentioned above, for this purpose, T2N could be extended by incorporating stochastic search algorithms (Foster et al., 1993; Goldman et al., 2001; Weaver and Wearne, 2008; Rathour and Narayanan, 2014; Mishra and Narayanan, 2017), which would allow users to generate multiple randomized models with different biophysical and morphological parameters leading to similar electrophysiological behavior.
evidence: This is a stated direction for future development.

claim: Generating multiple randomized models would help to reveal which combinations of channel properties and dendritic arborization support robustness of GC function.
source: This would help to reveal which combinations of channel properties and dendritic arborization support robustness of GC function.
evidence: This is a stated benefit of the proposed future work.

claim: It would be interesting to employ T2N and the new GC model to stochastically generate many biophysically distinct GC models with variable location-dependent channel expression as well as variable full dendritic morphologies.
source: It would be interesting to employ a similar approach and use T2N and our new GC model with the updated layer-specific composition of ionic channels to stochastically generate many biophysically distinct GC models with variable location-dependent channel expression as well as variable full dendritic morphologies (Schneider et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a stated direction for future research.

claim: Simulations and analyses in large collections of detailed conductance-based GC models might contribute to the identification of subcellular mechanisms of degeneracy.
source: Simulations and analyses in such large collections of detailed conductance-based GC models might contribute to the identification of subcellular mechanisms of degeneracy.
evidence: This is a stated potential outcome of future research.

claim: This approach would show whether disparate dendrite and channel parameters may lead to identical GC electrophysiology.
source: Specifically, this approach would show whether disparate dendrite and channel parameters, including dendrite length and branching as well as gradients in channel densities, kinetics, voltage-dependence or intracellular milieu may lead to identical GC electrophysiology.
evidence: This is a stated potential outcome of future research.

claim: T2N will be useful to generalize such analyses also to other cell types.
source: T2N will be useful to generalize such analyses also to other cell types.
evidence: This is a stated potential application of T2N.
